text:
alex: Quick async check — PR #8426 changed stop-sequence precedence and I noticed a canary oddity: when streaming with high temperature/top_p, responses sometimes include a partial stop token and then stream ends mid-token. Is that a runtime bug or expected due to sampling?

karim: Hmm, can you paste the exact request you used?

alex: Repro snippet: ```json
{
  "model": "redwood-inc/turbo-lite",
  "prompt": "Write a short haiku:",
  "max_tokens": 50,
  "temperature": 0.92,
  "top_p": 0.95,
  "stop": ["\\n\\n"],
  "logprobs": 5,
  "stream": true
}
```

sophia: Thanks. I think this is two related things: sampling overshoot + streaming chunk boundary handling. In sampling overshoot we can generate tokens that only *complete* the stop sequence when combined across multiple tokens. If runtime checks stop only at token boundaries but streaming flushes partial chunks, you can see a fragment.

ben: Also note we intentionally omit per-token logprobs in early streaming events to keep payload small — full logprobs are attached to the final non-stream event today. That can look like "missing logprobs then final has them".

alex: Right, that matches what I'm seeing — partial text first, then final event with no logprobs sometimes. For API contract clarity we should document streaming semantics: when logprobs are requested with stream=true we either (A) emit best-effort per-chunk logprobs (may be partial) or (B) guarantee logprobs only in final event. Which do we want?

karim: My vote: keep backward compatibility (B) as default, and add an opt-in `stream_logprobs: true` param that tries to include per-token logprobs in streaming chunks. Add strong caveats about increased bandwidth and possible partials.

sophia: Agreed. Also for stop handling we should add a `stop_strategy` setting: `token_boundary` (current), `substring` (check across buffer) and `greedy_strip` (post-process to ensure stop removed even if matched across tokens). Default remains `token_boundary` to avoid perf regressions.

alex: Sounds good. Can we get an API contract doc section + small runtime change? @ben can you file a follow-up PR to docs? I can prep the runtime patch but want a quick review.

ben: Filed docs PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/docs/pulls/2915 — added section under "Streaming semantics".

karim: Runtime patch idea in draft PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/serving/pulls/5437 — implements `stream_logprobs` flag and `stop_strategy` enum. Note: default path unchanged. Need eng-ml review for sampling correctness and perf tests.

alex: Pinged reviewers on PR 5437. @sophia can you sanity-check the sampling unit tests? Also would like a small canary — if deploy-bot can spin a canary for the change?

deploy-bot: Canary deploy started for serving/pull/5437 -> canary-redwood-2 (note: this will run on dedicated GPU pool).

sophia: I'll run the sampling unit tests today and add a small property-based test for stop sequences across token boundaries. If all green I'll approve.

karim: One more edge: what happens when `max_tokens` interacts with stop across tokens? If a stop completes *after* max_tokens truncated, we need to define whether we prioritize max_tokens (truncate) or stop (extend to include stop). Current contract: max_tokens hard cap — we should keep that but document the truncation behavior.

alex: Good call. Document: max_tokens is a hard upper bound; stop may shorten generation but never extends it. I'll add that to the docs PR.

ben: Thx. If reviewers approve today, we can canary for 4 hours and roll to prod tomorrow. :thumbsup:

alex: Thanks all — I'll assemble a brief release note for api-changes and ping support so they can expect customer questions about streaming logprobs.

sophia: Acked.

karim: Leaving follow-ups: 1) eng-ml review on PR 5437, 2) sophia adds tests, 3) alex updates docs and release note, 4) canary monitor for latency/bandwidth regressions.

alex: Ok closing this thread — please update status on PRs.
